title: Vulcan rocket fails during launch, dealing major blow to SpaceX competitors
gist: ULA's Vulcan rocket failed on its first Amazon Leo mission (40 satellites lost), ULA's first total mission failure since 2006, with sources pointing to the BE-4-powered booster stage. The grounding hits Amazon Leo's Starlink challenge, Space Force launch assurance and potentially Blue Origin's New Glenn and NASA's Artemis plans, while deepening dependence on SpaceX just as Falcon 9 heads toward retirement.

insights.claim: ULA's Vulcan rocket failed on its 15 November launch, losing 40 Amazon Leo broadband satellites; it was the first total mission failure for United Launch Alliance since its 2006 formation from the Boeing and Lockheed Martin rocket divisions.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Breaks ULA's flawless mission record, a core selling point for national security launch contracts.
insights.quote: This was the first total mission failure for United Launch Alliance since its formation in 2006

insights.claim: Multiple sources indicate the Vulcan anomaly originated in the booster stage, not the Centaur V upper stage or solid rocket boosters, though it is unclear whether the two Blue Origin BE-4 engines or propellant feed hardware were at fault.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: If BE-4 is implicated, the failure propagates to Blue Origin's New Glenn and its customers.
insights.locator: Multiple sources told Ars the anomaly

insights.claim: Vulcan's BE-4 main engines burned at least 30 seconds past their planned shutdown near the five-minute mark, a possible sign the booster stage underperformed and tried to compensate, followed by a spin through Centaur V separation.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Overburn telemetry points toward a booster performance problem; watch the investigation's root-cause findings.

insights.claim: Vulcan had already suffered solid rocket booster failures on two of its four prior flights, each triggering monthslong reviews, so a new booster-stage failure is expected to ground the rocket for an indefinite period.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Expect a long stand-down; ULA's manifest of Amazon and Space Force missions slips.
insights.locator: Vulcan is no stranger to close calls

insights.claim: Amazon has 37 more Vulcan launches reserved, each meant to carry 40+ Amazon Leo satellites, making the grounding of its primary launch provider a bigger problem than the 40 satellites lost.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Amazon Leo's constellation build-out and service timeline are now at risk of material delay.

insights.claim: The Amazon Leo constellation has 396 satellites in orbit versus a planned 3,292 first-generation spacecraft, while Amazon has built its 1,000th satellite, meaning more than half of manufactured satellites sit in storage awaiting launch.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Launch, not manufacturing, is Amazon's binding constraint versus Starlink; capital is tied up in grounded inventory.
insights.locator: The Amazon Leo constellation today consists of 396 satellites

insights.claim: Amazon Leo is positioned as the first head-to-head consumer satellite broadband competitor to SpaceX's Starlink, unlike OneWeb whose model sells capacity to telcos.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Launch delays extend Starlink's uncontested consumer market lead.
insights.locator: Amazon is setting up its service

insights.claim: Amazon's alternative launch capacity is limited: Arianespace holds 24 Amazon launches (three flown), New Glenn's pad is offline after a May ground-test explosion, and Amazon has 10 remaining Falcon 9 missions but likely cannot buy more as SpaceX retires the rocket.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Near-term Amazon Leo deployment hinges on Ariane 6 and existing Falcon 9 slots.
insights.locator: Amazon made launch bookings with Europe’s Arianespace

insights.claim: Amazon's past launch woes forced it to contract SpaceX, owned by Jeff Bezos' chief competitor in satellite broadband and launch, to deploy Amazon Leo satellites on Falcon 9.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Amazon funding its main rival's launch business is a structural disadvantage.

insights.claim: New Glenn uses a BE-4 variant similar to Vulcan's, and a faulty valve on a BE-4 caused the New Glenn ground-test explosion in May; if a BE-4 caused the Vulcan failure, New Glenn's planned return to flight early next year could slip.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: A shared-engine root cause would delay two heavy launchers at once, compounding constraints for Amazon, Space Force and NASA.
insights.locator: What’s more, the New Glenn rocket uses

insights.claim: Blue Origin's lunar lander test flights for NASA's Artemis program, backlogged on New Glenn for next year, could be pushed back further if the BE-4 is found at fault in the Vulcan failure.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Artemis crewed lunar timelines are exposed to the Vulcan investigation outcome.
insights.locator: Blue Origin’s New Glenn, once it returns to flight

themes.theme: National security launch dependence on SpaceX

insights.claim: Vulcan is contracted to launch roughly half of US military national security space missions in the next few years, so its grounding will push the Pentagon to further increase its heavy dependence on SpaceX.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Expect more Space Force mission swaps to SpaceX, strengthening SpaceX's government revenue and leverage.
insights.quote: Expect more Space Force rocket swaps after Vulcan’s errant launch Sunday.
insights.locator: Expect more Space Force rocket swaps

insights.claim: Earlier Vulcan delays already forced the Space Force to move six national security launches from ULA to SpaceX, with ULA receiving a future SpaceX mission in exchange.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Precedent for mission reallocation; more swaps are the likely response now.
insights.locator: Vulcan’s earlier delays forced Space Force officials

insights.claim: SpaceX is rapidly transitioning from Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy to Starship for Starlink and orbiting AI compute platforms, but has not revealed plans to certify Starship for national security missions, a multi-year process, creating a potential US assured-access gap.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: US national security launch could face a capacity squeeze if Vulcan and New Glenn falter while Falcon retires.
insights.locator: But SpaceX has made it clear

insights.claim: NASA selected a version of ULA's Centaur upper stage to replace a more expensive, unproven Boeing upper stage on the Space Launch System, aiming to fly it on crewed lunar missions as soon as 2028, so NASA will want to rule out a Centaur V role in the failure.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Any Centaur finding would ripple into SLS and Artemis schedules.
insights.locator: NASA’s lunar program has another important link

insights.claim: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman publicly backed ULA after the failure, signaling the agency views ULA as strategically indispensable.
insights.speaker: Stephen Clark
insights.so_what: Government support reduces the risk of ULA losing contracts despite the failure.
insights.quote: Artemis, Moon Base, and the nation need ULA.
